text: EXPLAIN shows PostgreSQL's planned strategy without running the query. EXPLAIN ANALYZE actually runs it and reports what really happened, next to what the planner estimated — and that gap is often the most useful thing in the whole plan.

Each line shows a cost estimate in planner units, and with ANALYZE, an actual time and row count. A Nested Loop's inner scan running once per outer row shows up right there as loops equal to the outer row count.

Seq Scan reads every row. Index Scan jumps straight to matches. Nested Loop probes one side per row from the other, efficient when the outer side is small. Hash Join builds an in-memory hash table for larger, similarly-sized inputs.

When actual rows differs wildly from the estimate, that's usually stale statistics or a misprediction, and it's often the real root cause behind a bad plan. Next up: PostgreSQL's richer index type ecosystem.
